description: Formation of hard surfaced area for the parking of up to 25 Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGVs) (Retrospective application)
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of the provision of HGV parking, represents inappropriate development within the Green Belt. The applicant has failed to demonstrate that there are any very special circumstances that clearly outweigh the harm to the Green Belt by reason of inappropriateness, and any other harm resulting from the proposal. Insufficient evidence has been provided to demonstrate a specific locational need for the proposed use or that a sequential assessment of alternative, less harmful sites has been undertaken. Furthermore, the site is isolated, with a Public Transport Accessibility Level (PTAL) of 0, and has poor accessibility to the strategic road network, contrary to the principles of locating development in sustainable locations. The proposal is therefore contrary to Paragraphs 110, 115 and 155 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G2 of the London Plan (2021), Policy EM2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 - Strategic Policies (2012), and Poli

The proposed development would result in the movement of Heavy Goods Vehicles along the narrow western section of Newyears Green Lane, which is unsuitable for such traffic. This would give rise to conditions prejudicial to highway safety. The site also has a Public Transport Accessibility Level of 0, with no safe or convenient walking or cycling routes, and is therefore located in an unsustainable location that would encourage travel by private motor vehicle. The proposal fails to promote sustainable transport modes and would conflict with the aims of the Policy 9 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policies T1, T2, and T4 of The London Plan (2021), and Policies DMT 1, DMT 2, DMT 5, and DMT 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020).

The applicant has failed to submit a Statutory Biodiversity Metric or Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment to demonstrate that the proposed development would deliver the required minimum 10 per cent net gain in biodiversity value in accordance with the Environment Act 2021. In the absence of this information, the Local Planning Authority is unable to assess the likely ecological impacts of the proposal or determine whether appropriate mitigation or enhancements would be secured. The proposal is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020), which seek to conserve and enhance biodiversity and secure measurable net gains.

In dealing with the application, the Council has implemented the National Planning Policy Framework requirement to work with the applicant positively and proactively. We have made available detailed advice through our statutory policies from the Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, and offering a full pre-application advice service.

We have, however, been unable to seek solutions to problems arising from the application as the proposal is contrary to our statutory policies, and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
